marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q001.takeaway: In a typical movement, the origin is the relatively fixed muscle attachment and the insertion moves toward it during contraction.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q001.displayText:
In a typical movement, the origin is the relatively fixed muscle attachment and the insertion moves toward it during contraction.

The origin of the muscle is fixed, while the insertion moves during contraction.

Skeletal muscles exert their force on bones through tendon attachments; the generated force helps produce movement or maintain posture.
emphasis: In a typical movement, the origin is the relatively fixed muscle attachment and the insertion moves toward it during contraction

rationales.a: The origin is generally the fixed attachment; the insertion typically moves.
rationales.b: The insertion is generally mobile during contraction, not fixed.
rationales.c: At least one attachment usually moves; both are not invariably fixed.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q002.takeaway: Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated; smooth muscle cells generally have one nucleus.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q002.displayText:
Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated; smooth muscle cells generally have one nucleus.

Skeletal muscles are multinucleated, while smooth muscles are uninucleated.

The three major muscle types are skeletal muscle, smooth muscle and cardiac muscle.
emphasis: Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated; smooth muscle cells generally have one nucleus

rationales.a: Smooth and cardiac muscle cells have a plasma membrane (sarcolemma), so this is true.
rationales.b: Intercalated discs are absent from skeletal and smooth muscle; this statement is true.
rationales.d: Smooth and cardiac muscle are under autonomic regulation, so this statement is true.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q003.takeaway: Endomysium surrounds each individual muscle fiber; perimysium surrounds fascicles and epimysium the whole muscle.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q003.displayText:
Endomysium surrounds each individual muscle fiber; perimysium surrounds fascicles and epimysium the whole muscle.

Muscle fibres are surrounded by a delicate connective-tissue network called endomysium.

Endomysium surrounds individual muscle fibers; perimysium surrounds bundles of muscle fibers (fasciculi); epimysium surrounds the whole muscle or muscle groups.

The endomysial, perimysial and epimysial layers fuse where muscles connect to adjacent structures such as tendons, aponeuroses and fasciae.
emphasis: Endomysium surrounds each individual muscle fiber; perimysium surrounds fascicles and epimysium the whole muscle

rationales.a: Endomysium surrounds single fibers, not whole muscle groups.
rationales.c: Perimysium surrounds fascicles; epimysium encloses the whole muscle group.
rationales.d: Perimysium encloses fascicles rather than individual muscle fibers.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q004.takeaway: Rectus abdominis has parallel fasciculi; deltoid, rectus femoris and tibialis anterior have oblique/pennate arrangements.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q004.displayText:
Rectus abdominis has parallel fasciculi; deltoid, rectus femoris and tibialis anterior have oblique/pennate arrangements.

Rectus abdominis contains parallel fasciculi; the other listed muscles have oblique fasciculi.

Muscle fasciculi may be parallel to the line of pull, oblique to it, or arranged in a spiral/twisted pattern.

Parallel muscles can be quadrilateral, strap-like, strap-like with tendinous intersections, or fusiform.
emphasis: Rectus abdominis has parallel fasciculi; deltoid, rectus femoris and tibialis anterior have oblique/pennate arrangements

rationales.a: Deltoid is multipennate, with fibers running obliquely to its tendon.
rationales.b: Rectus femoris is bipennate rather than parallel-fibered.
rationales.d: Tibialis anterior has a circumpennate arrangement, not parallel fasciculi.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q005.takeaway: Each trapezius is a broad triangular muscle; the paired muscles together resemble a trapezium.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q005.displayText:
Each trapezius is a broad triangular muscle; the paired muscles together resemble a trapezium.

Trapezius individually is a flat, triangular muscle extending over the back of the neck and upper thorax. Paired trapezius muscles resemble a trapezium, which gives the muscle its name.

Oblique-fiber muscles include triangular and pennate patterns. Pennate subtypes include unipennate, bipennate, multipennate and circumpennate (radial).
emphasis: Each trapezius is a broad triangular muscle; the paired muscles together resemble a trapezium

rationales.a: Quadrangular does not describe the outline of one trapezius muscle.
rationales.c: Multipennate describes fiber arrangement, not the overall shape asked here.
rationales.d: Fusiform muscles are spindle-shaped, unlike the flat triangular trapezius.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q006.takeaway: Pectoralis major has a spiral fiber arrangement as its clavicular and sternocostal fibers twist toward the humerus.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q006.displayText:
Pectoralis major has a spiral fiber arrangement as its clavicular and sternocostal fibers twist toward the humerus.

The muscle marked X is pectoralis major, a spiral muscle.

Spiral muscles have a twisted arrangement; pectoralis major sternocostal fibers and latissimus dorsi undergo about a 180° twist between attachments, while supinator winds obliquely around the proximal radius.

Cruciate is a spiral subtype in which two or more muscle-fiber planes run in differing directions; sternocleidomastoid, masseter and adductor magnus are examples described by the source.
emphasis: Pectoralis major has a spiral fiber arrangement as its clavicular and sternocostal fibers twist toward the humerus

rationales.b: Multipennate describes multiple featherlike fascicle groups, not the twisting of pectoralis major.
rationales.c: Parallel fibers run along the muscle axis and do not account for the attachment-related twist.
rationales.d: Cruciate describes crossing fibers, not the spiral course of pectoralis major.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q007.takeaway: Tibialis anterior has oblique circumpennate fibers rather than parallel fibers.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q007.displayText:
Tibialis anterior has oblique circumpennate fibers rather than parallel fibers.

Tibialis anterior has oblique muscle fibers arranged in a circumpennate (radial) fashion rather than parallel fibers. Fibers arise from the walls of its osteofascial compartment and converge obliquely on a central tendon.

Sartorius, rectus abdominis and sternohyoid have parallel fibers.
emphasis: Tibialis anterior has oblique circumpennate fibers rather than parallel fibers

rationales.a: Sartorius is a long strap muscle with parallel fibers.
rationales.b: Rectus abdominis is a parallel-fibered strap muscle.
rationales.c: Sternohyoid is a straight strap muscle with parallel fibers.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q008.takeaway: A digastric muscle has two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon; digastric and omohyoid are examples.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q008.displayText:
A digastric muscle has two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon; digastric and omohyoid are examples.

A muscle with two bellies and an intervening tendon is a digastric muscle. Examples include digastric and omohyoid.

Diarthric muscles extend over two joints. Biaxial describes joints permitting movement in two axes.
emphasis: A digastric muscle has two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon; digastric and omohyoid are examples

rationales.a: Biceps denotes two heads of origin, not necessarily two bellies with an intervening tendon.
rationales.b: Diarthric describes a muscle acting across two joints, not belly-and-tendon structure.
rationales.d: Biaxial describes movement around two joint axes, not muscle architecture.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q009.takeaway: Dupuytren contracture thickens and contracts the palmar aponeurosis, a broad sheet-like tendon.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q009.displayText:
Dupuytren contracture thickens and contracts the palmar aponeurosis, a broad sheet-like tendon.

The condition is Dupuytren's contracture, involving contracture of the flat broad sheet-like tendon called an aponeurosis and producing flexion deformity, especially of the ring and little fingers.

An aponeurosis is a pearly-white sheet of fibrous tissue replacing tendons in sheet-like muscles with broad attachment. It resembles tendon histologically and is sparsely supplied by blood vessels and nerves.

Examples include palmar and plantar aponeuroses, anterior abdominal aponeuroses, anterior/posterior intercostal membranes and the scalp galea aponeurotica.

A retinaculum is a strong short broad fibrous band retaining tendons; a raphe is a linear fibrous band formed by interdigitation of tendinous/aponeurotic ends; fascia is a generic term for visible connective-tissue sheaths or sheets.
emphasis: Dupuytren contracture thickens and contracts the palmar aponeurosis, a broad sheet-like tendon

rationales.a: A retinaculum holds tendons in place at a joint; it is not the palmar sheet involved.
rationales.b: A raphe is a linear seam formed where aponeuroses meet, not the broad palmar fascia sheet.
rationales.d: Fascia is a broad connective tissue term, but the named dense tendon sheet here is an aponeurosis.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q010.takeaway: The Z disc lies in the middle of the I band; the A band spans thick filaments and overlap zones.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q010.displayText:
The Z disc lies in the middle of the I band; the A band spans thick filaments and overlap zones.

The Z disc (Krause membrane) lies in the middle of the I band, not the A band.

The A band contains both thick and thin filaments; the H band within it contains only thick filaments and the M line lies centrally. The I band contains only thin filaments and has the Z disc centrally.

The segment of a myofibril between two Z discs is the sarcomere.
emphasis: The Z disc lies in the middle of the I band; the A band spans thick filaments and overlap zones

rationales.a: The A band contains thick filaments and overlapping thin filaments, so this is true.
rationales.b: The I band contains thin filaments without thick filaments.
rationales.c: The H zone contains thick filaments only.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q011.takeaway: Autonomic efferents control vascular smooth muscle; somatic alpha and gamma motor neurons supply skeletal muscle structures.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q011.displayText:
Autonomic efferents control vascular smooth muscle; somatic alpha and gamma motor neurons supply skeletal muscle structures.

Autonomic efferents supply vascular smooth muscle fibers.

Every skeletal muscle is supplied by a mixed motor nerve containing motor and sensory fibers. Extrafusal muscle fibers receive large myelinated α-efferents; intrafusal spindle fibers receive small myelinated γ-efferents; vascular smooth muscle receives fine unmyelinated autonomic efferents.
emphasis: Autonomic efferents control vascular smooth muscle; somatic alpha and gamma motor neurons supply skeletal muscle structures

rationales.a: Alpha motor axons are large and myelinated, not small unmyelinated fibers.
rationales.c: Gamma motor neurons supply intrafusal fibers, not extrafusal muscle fibers.
rationales.d: Alpha motor neurons innervate extrafusal fibers; gamma motor neurons innervate intrafusal fibers.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q012.takeaway: Flower-spray endings are secondary group II sensory endings on muscle-spindle nuclear chain fibers.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q012.displayText:
Flower-spray endings are secondary group II sensory endings on muscle-spindle nuclear chain fibers.

Flower spray endings in muscle spindles are secondary sensory nerve endings.

Muscle spindles receive thickly myelinated Ia and thinly myelinated II afferents. Primary Ia annulospiral endings lie in the central nuclear region, while secondary II flower-spray endings lie on either side of the nuclei.

The Golgi tendon organ is supplied by large myelinated Ib afferents. Connective-tissue sheaths receive fine myelinated and unmyelinated axons carrying pain and other sensations.
emphasis: Flower-spray endings are secondary group II sensory endings on muscle-spindle nuclear chain fibers

rationales.a: Beta efferents are not flower-spray sensory endings.
rationales.b: Gamma motor endings adjust spindle sensitivity and are not sensory flower-spray endings.
rationales.c: Primary group Ia endings are annulospiral, wrapping around the central region of spindle fibers.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q013.takeaway: A small motor unit contains about 5–10 muscle fibers, enabling fine graded control.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q013.displayText:
A small motor unit contains about 5–10 muscle fibers, enabling fine graded control.

A small motor unit has 5-10 muscle fibers.

A motor unit (myone) is one α motor neuron together with all muscle fibers it supplies. Fine-control muscles have fewer fibers per neuron; gross-movement muscles may have many.

The source describes small motor units (5-10 fibers) in fine-movement muscles such as extraocular muscles, and large motor units (100-2000 fibers) in gross-movement muscles such as proximal limb muscles.
emphasis: A small motor unit contains about 5–10 muscle fibers, enabling fine graded control

rationales.b: Ten to one hundred fibers is larger than the stated small-unit range.
rationales.c: Hundreds to a thousand fibers typify larger units for gross force, not fine control.
rationales.d: Thousands of fibers would be a very large motor unit.

marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q014.takeaway: Flexor carpi ulnaris is supplied only by the ulnar nerve, so it is not a hybrid muscle.
marrow__ANAT_CH61_Q014.displayText:
Flexor carpi ulnaris is supplied only by the ulnar nerve, so it is not a hybrid muscle.

Flexor carpi ulnaris is not a hybrid muscle because it is supplied by a single nerve (ulnar nerve).

A composite/hybrid muscle is supplied by two different nerves with different root values and usually has different sets of fibers with separate nerve supplies.

Examples listed include brachialis, pectoralis major, iliopsoas, subscapularis, biceps femoris, adductor magnus, digastric, flexor pollicis brevis, flexor digitorum profundus, pectineus, opponens pollicis and trapezius.
emphasis: Flexor carpi ulnaris is supplied only by the ulnar nerve, so it is not a hybrid muscle

rationales.a: Flexor digitorum profundus has dual innervation: median/anterior interosseous and ulnar nerves.
rationales.b: Biceps femoris has different nerve supply to its long and short heads (tibial and common fibular divisions).
rationales.c: Pectineus may receive femoral and obturator/accessory obturator nerve supply.
